name: packmol
desc: Packing optimization for molecular dynamics simulations
why: Packs molecules into boxes for molecular dynamics setups, real science, though a niche preprocessing step.

brief.what_it_is: Packmol is a command-line program that builds starting coordinates for molecular dynamics simulations by placing copies of molecules into a region of space without overlaps. You supply a coordinate file for one molecule of each type (PDB, TINKER, or XYZ), the number of copies of each, and spatial constraints such as being inside a box, sphere, cylinder, or above a plane. It writes a coordinate file of the packed system. The user guide's example packs 2000 water molecules into a 40 Å cube from a short text input file.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says PACKMOL "creates an initial point for molecular dynamics simulations by packing molecules in defined regions of space" so that short-range repulsive interactions do not disrupt the simulation. It also says that the variety of constraints makes it easy to build ordered systems such as lamellar, spherical, or tubular lipid layers.
brief.how_it_works: The input file lists each molecule type with a number of copies and constraint keywords (inside/outside box, sphere, ellipsoid, cylinder, plane, and others). The tolerance keyword sets the minimum atom-atom distance, which is 2.0 Å for typical all-atom systems. The program optimizes the positions and rotations of the molecules to satisfy the distance and region constraints, and it reports a final objective value and maximum violations when it succeeds. The guide says it is a first-pass coordinate generator and that the output should go through minimization and equilibration afterward.

commands_seen.context: Unpacks the Packmol source tarball (the user guide's example version is 21.0.0); creates a packmol directory.
Moves into the unpacked source directory before building.
Builds the packmol executable from source, per the user guide's compile instructions.
Fallback if the build fails: the configure script tries to find a suitable compiler. The guide says to run chmod +x ./configure first.
Runs Packmol by redirecting the input file on stdin (option 1).
Runs Packmol with command-line arguments (option 2, from v21.1.0 onward); -o is optional and overrides the output name in the input file.
Input-file keyword setting the minimum distance between atoms of different molecules; the guide calls 2.0 a good value for room-temperature systems in Angstroms.
Input-file keyword that turns on orthorhombic periodic boundary conditions for a 30x30x60 Å box.
Input-file keyword that writes a restart file so a later run can build on this packing.
Bundled helper script that generates a Packmol input file to solvate a large molecule such as a protein with water and ions. Runs with no arguments to print its options.

brief.install_notes: Requires a C/Fortran toolchain to build from source: download packmol-21.0.0.tar.gz from the homepage, unpack, run make (or ./configure then make). The guide says most users should use the Julia wrapper (Packmol.jl), which needs no compilation and works on all platforms. Windows users are advised to use Packmol.jl. No account or license acceptance is mentioned. Not verified: whether the Homebrew formula also installs solvate.tcl or other utilities.
brief.standout: Constraints are declared as geometric regions (inside or outside a cylinder, sphere, or gaussian surface, above or below a plane, per-atom selections), so you can describe a lipid vesicle or a membrane interface in a few lines. The restart-file mechanism lets very large systems be built in stages.
brief.status: Maintained as far as the pages show: the user guide refers to version 21.0.0 and mentions a 21.1.0 feature, and the homepage links a version history. I did not find a release date or commit date, so recency is not confirmed.
brief.caveats: Packmol is a preprocessing step, not a simulation engine; the guide says the output needs minimization and equilibration. The guide notes that a memory "Killed" error requires editing maxatom in sizes.i and recompiling. The 'Command not found' fix is ./packmol or adding the directory to PATH. Packing can fail to converge; the guide suggests tweaking discale, maxit, movefrac, or other settings. The guide says Windows users should use the Julia wrapper instead of the source build. The first homepage fetch returned only an 'Opening page...' stub; the content came from the m3g.github.io mirror. The guide also points to an older download host (m3g.iqm.unicamp.br), so links may be inconsistent. License was not checked.
quotes: PACKMOL creates an initial point for molecular dynamics simulations by packing molecules in defined regions of space.
The user must provide only the coordinates of one molecule of each type, the number of molecules of each type and the spatial constraints that each type of molecule must satisfy.
Always download the latest version of Packmol to ensure all features are available.
